learningObjectives.title: Structure and function of the brain

questions.q: The central nervous system (CNS) is made up of which two structures?
questions.explain: The CNS consists of the brain and the spinal cord, which coordinate the body's activity.

questions.q: Which type of neuron carries electrical impulses from the CNS to effectors such as muscles?
questions.explain: Motor neurons transmit signals from the CNS to effectors such as muscles and glands.

questions.q: Receptors in the skin detect heat from a hot surface. Which type of neuron carries this information towards the CNS?
questions.explain: Sensory neurons carry impulses from receptors towards the central nervous system.

questions.q: What is the main role of adrenaline during the fight or flight response?
options: It prepares the body for action by increasing heart rate
It slows the heart rate to conserve energy
It stores memories in the brain
questions.explain: Adrenaline, released by the adrenal glands, prepares the body for action by raising heart rate and breathing.

questions.q: Which branch of the autonomic nervous system is activated during the fight or flight response?
questions.explain: The sympathetic branch triggers the fight or flight response, arousing the body for action.

questions.q: What is the name of the tiny gap between two neurons across which messages are passed?
questions.explain: The synapse is the small gap between neurons through which chemical messages travel.

questions.q: During synaptic transmission, how is the message carried across the gap between two neurons?
options: By chemical neurotransmitters that diffuse across the synapse
By an electrical spark jumping the gap
questions.explain: Neurotransmitters are released into the synapse and diffuse across to bind with receptors on the next neuron.

questions.q: Jae is suddenly startled by a loud bang and notices her heart pounding and her breathing quicken. Which response best explains these changes?
questions.explain: A sudden threat triggers the fight or flight response, increasing heart rate and breathing to prepare for action.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the function of the cerebellum?
questions.explain: The cerebellum is mainly involved in coordinating voluntary movement and maintaining balance.

questions.q: The cerebrum is divided into four lobes. Which of the following is one of these lobes?
questions.explain: The four lobes of the cerebrum are the frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes.

questions.q: What is the main role of the parasympathetic branch of the autonomic nervous system?
options: Returning the body to a calm, resting state
Preparing the body for emergency action
Carrying sensory information to the brain
questions.explain: The parasympathetic branch calms the body and returns it to a resting state after arousal.

questions.q: A patient suffers damage to the cerebellum after an accident. Which difficulty are they most likely to experience?
options: Problems with balance and coordinating movement
questions.explain: Because the cerebellum coordinates movement and balance, damage to it typically causes problems in these areas.

questions.q: In which lobe is the motor area, which controls voluntary movement, located?
questions.explain: The motor area, controlling voluntary movement, is located in the frontal lobe.

questions.q: The visual area, which processes information from the eyes, is found in which lobe?
questions.explain: The visual area is located in the occipital lobe at the back of the brain.

questions.q: The somatosensory area processes sensations such as touch, pressure and temperature. In which lobe is it located?
questions.explain: The somatosensory area, which processes touch and other skin sensations, is found in the parietal lobe.

questions.q: After a stroke, Mr Ford can no longer see properly even though his eyes are undamaged. Damage to which brain area is the most likely cause?
options: The visual area in the occipital lobe
The motor area in the frontal lobe
The auditory area in the temporal lobe
questions.explain: If the eyes are healthy but sight is lost, the damage is most likely to the visual area in the occipital lobe.

questions.q: The case study of Phineas Gage is used to show the effects of damage to which part of the brain?
questions.explain: An iron rod damaged Gage's frontal lobe, which was followed by marked changes in his personality.

questions.q: What does an fMRI scan measure in order to show which parts of the brain are active?
options: Changes in blood flow and oxygen use
The electrical activity of single neurons
The amount of neurotransmitter in a synapse
questions.explain: fMRI detects changes in blood flow and oxygen use, which increase in more active brain regions.

questions.q: Which scanning technique uses X-rays to produce a detailed image of the brain's structure?
questions.explain: A CT (computed tomography) scan uses X-rays to build up a detailed image of brain structure.

questions.q: A researcher wants to see which brain areas become active while a participant completes a memory task. Which scanning technique is most suitable?
questions.explain: An fMRI scan shows brain activity during a task, making it ideal for observing areas active during a memory task.
